subject.title: feat(gateway): durable user profiles with email aliases and avatars

question: Should OpenClaw adopt durable shared-gateway user profiles, aliases, avatars, and their public gateway/CLI administration API as the next supported identity-program contract?
rationale: This PR is additive and coherent, but its persistent schema and public protocol establish a long-lived product and compatibility boundary that tests alone cannot select.

options.title: Sponsor the durable-profile contract
options.body: Approve this slice as part of the canonical identity program after adding real authenticated gateway proof and completing normal review.

options.title: Narrow the contract first
options.body: Retain only the storage seam or selected APIs until the intended identity-management and privacy surface is settled.

options.title: Defer profiles
options.body: Keep the existing presence and attribution work while postponing durable profiles and avatar administration to a later product decision.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the durable-profile contract
recommendation.body: Approve this slice as part of the canonical identity program after adding real authenticated gateway proof and completing normal review.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the demonstrated contributor across the merged identity-train slices and this proposed durable-profile implementation.
